title: Sustainable Mineral Resources and Resource Security: A Systematic Review of Financialisation, Price Volatility, and Capital Allocation
content: The low-carbon transition has shifted strategic dependence from fossil fuels to critical mineral resources (lithium, cobalt, nickel, copper, and rare earth elements). However, mineral resource scarcity, extractive-industry concentration, and geopolitical bottlenecks amplify price volatility and threaten sustainable resource security. Concurrently, derivatives, exchange-traded funds (ETFs), and institutional flows accelerate the financialisation of strategic resources. Following PRISMA 2020, this systematic review synthesises research on mineral resource governance, fi-nancialisation, and capital allocation across four clusters: (1) financialisation of mineral resources and price discovery; (2) volatility spillovers across primary and secondary resource markets; (3) portfolio strategies and industrial hedging; and (4) ESG risk pricing, mining cost of capital, and circular resource economy finance. Central to this study is the Green Transition Capital Alloca-tion Paradox: whereas liquid derivatives facilitate risk transfer, speculative financialisation in shallow markets amplifies tail-risk contagion, inflating mining cost of capital (WACC), rationing equity for junior explorers, and delaying capital expenditure (CAPEX) in primary extraction and urban mining. These frictions compound physical bottlenecks, prolonging 10–16-year mine lead times and leaving 50% of displaced copper unreplaced via price-rebound effects. Finally, a policy agenda addresses explainable AI forecasting, secondary-resource derivatives, and state-backed de-risking instruments.
